summary: Jefferson Co., OR: tree-platform lookout (1930/1934) with a tower from 1948 or 1951, removed in 1965; the platform tree was still standing in the 1980s.

facts.design: Tree platform (1930 or 1934); tower either 53 ft (1948, Bend Bulletin) or 40-ft wooden L-4 (1951, FFLOS and Fire Lookout)
facts.status_note: Tower removed 1965; tree platform still standing in the 1980s, and the Forest Service later decided to remove it
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Deschutes National Forest

events.note: Tree platform built (Former Fire Lookout Sites, Fire Lookout); Forest Lookouts gives 1934
Tree with platform established as a secondary lookout point (Forest Lookouts)
Tower built in a tree with a tent at its foot; patrolled by Allen Madsen of Camp Sherman (Bend Bulletin, June 25, 1941)
Paul Striebel was fireman; lookout in the top of a 73-foot tree
53-foot lookout tower erected near Fly Lake; first lookout Paul Striebel (Bend Bulletin, Aug 25, 1948)
40-foot wooden L-4 tower replaced the tree platform (FFLOS and Fire Lookout)
Mr. and Mrs. Joseph Burns on duty (Bend Bulletin, June 17, 1953)
David Snow was lookout-fireman; last year the lookout was staffed
State highway contract for five miles of road to Fly Lake Lookout; Forest Service contract for the remaining four miles, starting at the lookout (April 17, 1968)
Registered August 24, 2010; nominated by Ray Kresek

corrections.why: 22.9 m is 75 ft, the height the Forest Lookouts page gives for the 1941 tree lookout, not a tower. FFLOS and the Fire Lookout page both give a 40-foot wooden L-4 tower (1951). The Forest Lookouts page gives 53 feet for a 1948 tower, so the editor may prefer 16.2 m if that account is accepted.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts (Bend Bulletin, August 1948) says a 53-foot tower was erected near Fly Lake in 1948. FFLOS and the Fire Lookout page say a 40-foot wooden L-4 tower was put up in 1951. All three agree the tower was removed in 1965. The story reports both accounts.
FFLOS and the Fire Lookout page date the tree platform to 1930; Forest Lookouts gives 1934 for a tree with a platform as a secondary lookout point. The story gives both dates.

notes_for_editor: Brief height 22.9 m equals the 75-ft 1941 tree lookout and was corrected to the 40-ft tower. The 1948 53-ft tower (Forest Lookouts) and the 1951 40-ft tower (FFLOS, Fire Lookout) conflict; both are reported. The brief note that sources disagree on a tower versus a tree is answered: tree platforms, then towers. The 1934 entry is a secondary lookout point, not the first lookout. No source describes the site today and no current access information was found; the 1968 road reference is historical. No photos added.
